answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by weighting identity on verifiable open-source contribution history: merged commits, reviewed pull requests, and long-lived repository work form a public record no farm can fake overnight. A fresh identity sits at the nadir of trust until real contributions lift it toward the vertex, while a raven-like watcher, the open commit graph, exposes copy-paste histories instantly. Forging years of genuine collaboration costs more than the attack gains.
